problem: General video generators lack embodied physics (contact, rigid-body structure, action-consequence), while domain-specific embodied world models rely on robot-specific action representations (joint angles, waypoints) and cannot generalize across embodiments, tasks or scenarios.
motivation: Real-world robot training is costly and unsafe, so world models are needed as scalable simulators for data synthesis, policy evaluation and planning. Natural language is the most general action interface, so heterogeneous manipulation, driving, navigation and human-to-robot data can be trained jointly under one language-conditioned video model.
key_idea: Treat natural language as the unified action interface for a 20B double-stream MMDiT video world model with a frozen Qwen2.5-VL action encoder, trained on 8.6M action-language-mapped embodied and general video-text pairs (EWK) with a general-to-expert curriculum.
insight: The paper's evidence is benchmark-level: joint general and embodied training under one language interface gives top results on EWMBench (4.60 vs LVP 4.05) and DreamGen Bench (4.952), and perfect physics-adherence scores on WorldModelBench. There are no ablations isolating the contribution of the MLLM encoder, the multi-domain mixing or the curriculum, so those design claims are asserted rather than tested. Weakness on visual-quality metrics (PBench aesthetics and imaging, WorldModelBench common sense) is attributed by the authors to lower output resolution.
method: Double-Stream MMDiT with MLLM action encoding: 60 double-stream blocks (hidden size 3072, 24 heads, patch 2x2, ~20B params). A frozen Qwen2.5-VL (7B) provides last-layer hidden states as the action condition (understanding stream, via a trainable connector), and Wan-VAE latents form the generation stream. The two streams interact through joint attention at every block.
Asymmetric 3D RoPE: axis dims [16,56,56] for time/height/width, plus Scalable RoPE for varying resolution and duration; also supports multi-view concatenation without architectural changes.

Action-language mapping and five-layer annotation: heterogeneous actions from 20+ embodiments and 500+ action categories are converted to captions via Task Goal, Action Detail (explicit viewpoint), Physical Feedback, then a comprehensive (50-100 words) and a concise (15-30 words) caption, sampled 50/50 in training. An LLM judge, human review and iterative prompt refinement filter captions.

EWK dataset: 8.6M video-text pairs (200M+ frames), 30% general and 70% embodied. The embodied part comprises manipulation (~4.3M single-view plus ~1.6M multi-view concatenated), ~200K driving and navigation samples (Waymo, PhysicalAI-AD, Bench2Drive, Sekai, VLNVerse: 6,064 episodes over 134 scenes), and human-to-robot paired data (14 robot arms, MANO retargeting plus MuJoCo).

General+Expert progressive curriculum: pretraining jointly on T2I, T2V and TI2V over general data plus human egocentric data. SFT is a four-phase schedule (single-view, then multi-view, then multi-view concatenation, then complex and cross-domain tasks) with 70% embodied and 30% general data. Within the embodied portion manipulation is ~90% and driving and navigation ~5%. Flow-matching objective, first-frame timestep 0 for TI2V.

Scene2Robot: a multi-segment conditioning scheme for human-to-robot video editing. The input is a scene video with hands masked, a MuJoCo robot reference video and a generation segment. Condition segments are assigned t=0 and excluded from the loss, with each segment given its own RoPE temporal range.

setting.backbone: Qwen-RobotWorld: 60-layer double-stream MMDiT (20B) + frozen Qwen2.5-VL 7B encoder + Wan-VAE (trained from scratch/pretrained internally)
setting.training_data: EWK: 8.6M video-text pairs (200M+ frames): 30% general internet video/images, plus manipulation (20+ embodiments), driving (Waymo, PhysicalAI-AD, Bench2Drive, Sekai), indoor navigation (VLNVerse, 6K episodes) and human-to-robot data; pretraining on 200M+ general observation samples
setting.observation: Current frame(s) (first-frame conditioning, optionally multi-view concatenated) plus a text instruction
setting.action_space: Natural language instructions (comprehensive or concise); output is generated future video
setting.simulator: Not applicable for evaluation (video-generation benchmarks); Isaac Sim, CARLA and MuJoCo are used to produce training data

numbers_note: No embodied-navigation benchmark numbers are reported (no SR/SPL). Indoor navigation (VLNVerse) and driving results are qualitative only. The RoboTwin-IF zero-shot results are given only as figures.
results: Ranks 1st overall on EWMBench (4.60 vs LVP 4.05; HSD 0.566, +33% over LVP) and on DreamGen Bench (4.952 vs LVP 4.758). On WorldModelBench it is best among open-source models (8.99, 3rd overall behind Wan2.6 and Veo3), and on PBench best among open-source models (0.804). Visual quality (aesthetics 0.455, imaging 0.649) is relatively weak.
limitations: Lower output resolution hurts visual-quality scores (PBench aesthetics and imaging, WorldModelBench common sense).

No ablations isolating the MLLM encoder, the multi-domain mixing or the curriculum, and no quantitative results for navigation, driving, human-to-robot transfer or the claimed downstream applications (data synthesis, policy evaluation, planning).
Long-horizon behavior instruction following lags (GR1-Behavior IF 0.832 vs LVP 0.889).
